title: Foundation Form A — From a model to a defensible decision
review_type: Specialist author mathematical, computational, instructional and scoring review; root independently audits and alone integrates/accepts

format.conditions: Closed notes and solutions; basic nonprogrammable calculator; all model inputs and required normal quantile supplied

reviewed.prerequisites: Read the fixed assignment, current accepted curriculum/status, relevant Volume1 accounting/opportunity/real-value instruction, Volume2 contraction and constrained-allocation instruction, Volume3 loss/information/normal-coverage instruction, accepted Volume4 vintage/projection/validation/identification methods, and earlier volume assessment conventions. Seventeen chapter links cover all four accepted volumes. No future-volume method is required.
reviewed.reasoning: All twenty prompts and solutions were reviewed for their exact target, input conventions and scope. D1 distinguishes an incremental asset decision from financing, historical study expense, forgone rental receipts, accounting stocks and current liquidity. D2 proves a complete-interval contraction or IVT existence result, derives uniqueness and a geometric-tail bound, then handles a constrained allocation corner/interior transition and propagates numerical workload error to value. D3 constructs a joint probability law before updating, derives expected-loss choices and information values, prices a report-contingent invoice, and separates normal-pivot coverage from posterior statements. D4 freezes releases before aggregation/fitting, maintains firm-month keys and calendar changes, checks projection residuals, preserves selection/test timing, and identifies an absent large-firm zero-dose comparison.
reviewed.solutions: Four five-part questions have twenty matched complete solutions with explicit five-point scoring. The point allocations each total five and each domain totals twenty-five. Determinate answers include units and boundaries; open responses have concrete criteria and examples. Correct carried arithmetic receives follow-through credit while incompatible populations, dates, units and probabilistic interpretations do not receive reasoning credit.
reviewed.originality: Original cumulative transfer cases rather than reproduced examination questions: a machine-versus-rent comparison joins real/nominal valuation to time-zero financing and liquidity; a quadratic-feedback fixed point controls the level of a piecewise optimal allocation and its numerical-value error; information acquisition has a report-contingent invoice that differs from a universal fixed fee; a versioned firm-month regression has both a legitimate later revision and an illegitimate retrospectively relabeled forecast. Data, dates and parameter laws differ from Volume4 exams, and the distinct FormB mechanism allocation is preserved.
reviewed.proof_scope: The workload map's uniform Lipschitz bound and invariant complete domain are verified, not assumed from local numerical convergence. Fixed-point uniqueness is shown directly and the extraneous root is excluded by the domain. Tail bounds are derived from contracting increments; the smallest index passing a conservative bound is distinguished from actual convergence speed. Optimization existence, binding capacity, strict curvature, feasibility at both corners and the value-function transition are explicit. Normal confidence coverage follows the exact normal pivot, with the small 1.96-quantile rounding approximation acknowledged.
reviewed.sources: Reused stable methods and already inspected primary references through accepted chapter links. No new real-world economic, financial, legal, institutional or empirical assertion was introduced, so no new source retrieval or source-catalogue proposal was necessary. Synthetic releases are clearly not official observations, and rates/probabilities are assumptions rather than current facts. No external exam or source problem was copied.
reviewed.structure: Static fragment begins with h2#form-a, has no h1, contains four domain headings and twenty uniquely prefixed part/solution IDs, captioned tables, matching scoring paragraphs and balanced tags. No downloads, remote assets, framework or installation were added. Shared metadata/build/checkpoint, other assignments and publication remain root-owned and untouched.

validation.integration_api: check() returns JSON-serializable status, assessment, checks, results and limitations; standalone execution prints JSON with unsuccessful exit on a failed audit

root_preliminary_review.scope: Root reported reading the complete manuscript and all twenty solutions and independently tracing financial, contraction/allocation, Bayesian/normal and panel/holdout quantities.
root_preliminary_review.findings: No material correction requested during preliminary manuscript review. Final whole-package integration and acceptance remain root responsibilities.

limitations: This is internal specialist/root review, not independent human academic certification or evidence that the proposed timing/difficulty has been calibrated on learners.
The numerical checker supplements written proofs and economic interpretation; finite fixtures do not establish all possible model or program properties.

All financial operations, coefficients, probabilities and releases are synthetic. Actual investment suitability, source credibility, causal effects and predictive performance require further evidence.
The statistical coverage claim is conditional on fixed-sample iid normal observations with known variance; no posterior for the unknown mean is supplied.
The allocation's independent quadratic upper bound is a checker route; learners need only the taught derivative/curvature/boundary argument requested by the question.
No visual/mobile/print inspection was attempted; the recorded browser-policy restriction remains respected.
Root retains administration, mastery gates, cross-form review, practical/oral integration, shared build verification, final acceptance and publication.
handoff: Complete bounded foundation FormA package submitted for root integration. Only the three assigned FormA paths were written; no child agents, shared edits, commits or publication.
